question: Can the original two-window decoder produce static GS when only its continuous code is optimized towards the same initial GS, without changing the decoder or initial condition?
initialization: The previously saved Q-Former codes from repeated S0 input
training_target: S0 rendered at each target camera; S0 latent support and features; future states and moving reference excluded from every optimizer update
training_loss: full-image L1 + hand-ROI L1 + 0.1 * (balanced latent occupancy BCE + normalized latent feature L1)
evaluation: Frozen original motion Q code and current static code against same-camera S0 and true future codec references, view 0; compare old control at step 0; 18 future frames and videos at each checkpoint
success_interpretation: An optimized static code should yield a near-static image and GS state at both windows and all horizons; weighted MAE plus frame-by-frame visual review, not a numeric-only success claim
limitations: Two known training windows, one source video, one static-code initialization and limited budget. Optimizing codes uses target S0 and is not posterior training or AR. Failure does not prove impossibility. No independent GS cold replay or cross-video generalization.
